title: repro compare records the frozen set at the start commit and prints answer-found, false good and churn per area
goal: repro compare runs the frozen set at the run's start commit as well as at each instance's end and records per instance and area the answer-found count at start and end, the good verdicts without the answer (false good) at start and end and the verdict churn on rows of areas the instance did not research; the verdict a row is compared with is the one measured at the start commit, not repro_bench.csv's expect_verdict; a planted pair of instances in the compare part of test_bench.py proves each figure (no new test id)

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import bench_repro as b;m=[n for n in ['found_start', 'found_end', 'false_good_start', 'false_good_end', 'churn'] if n not in b.COMPARE_METRICS];print('missing',m);sys.exit(1 if m else 0)

notes: Merges the proposed draft ST-27slouvg (repro_bench.csv expect_verdict is the verdict measured at the start commit): the start commit's own verdicts replace the column as the baseline, and the file is not edited. Figures it would have shown (lessons analysis 3.2): answer found on the 14 common areas 15 at START against 58, 64 and 57; good with the answer 9 against 48, 51 and 47; rows of unresearched areas moved (pip 2 to 4 in instance 2). The compare functions it changes: eval_rows, agreement, compare_rows, compare (bench_repro.py), docs kb/_self/tools.md:24. Checks that pass before the work: the test selection pass before the work and are kept as guards (the change must keep them green); check 0 fails before the work and reads the goal. Each guard check named above as passing on the base passes before the work: it pins behaviour that must stay green (a test selection the work extends, the eval, the lint); the item's failing checks read its goal.
